# neo4j

Neo4j openCypher access through the official drivers (Python, Java, Go, JavaScript) - bounded, anchored, parameterized queries, and EXPLAIN/PROFILE plans imported as dumps (AllNodesScan, CartesianProduct, fan-out).

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-DATA-013` — Graph traversal/query without a limit (medium)

A Gremlin traversal with no limit()/range()/tail()/next()/count() on the chain, or an openCypher/SPARQL read without LIMIT (Neptune or Neo4j), returns an unbounded graph result — memory cost scales with the graph.


Remediation: Bound traversals with .limit(n)/.range(a,b) and add LIMIT to query strings.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/access-graph-gremlin.html

### `AF-GDB-004` — openCypher variable-length path without an upper bound (high)

A relationship pattern such as [*] or [*2..] has no maximum hop count; path enumeration explodes on dense neighborhoods.


Remediation: Declare an upper bound ([*1..3]) sized to the access pattern and keep a LIMIT.

Reference: https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/patterns/variable-length-patterns/

### `AF-GDB-005` — openCypher MATCH with no label or property anchor (medium)

A MATCH whose node patterns carry no label, no inline properties and no previously bound variable scans every node (Neptune explain shows label 'ALL').


Remediation: Anchor the pattern with a label and an indexed property, or reuse a bound variable.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/access-graph-opencypher-explain.html

### `AF-GDB-006` — openCypher disconnected patterns form a cartesian product (medium)

Comma-separated MATCH patterns that share no variable multiply their result sets; rows grow as the product of both sides.


Remediation: Connect the patterns through a shared variable or split them into separate queries.

Reference: https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/planning-and-tuning/operators/operators-detail/#query-plan-cartesian-product

### `AF-GDB-008` — Graph query text built by concatenation or interpolation (medium)

Query strings assembled with f-strings, format(), + or template literals open Gremlin/Cypher/SPARQL injection and defeat query-plan caching.


Remediation: Pass values as bindings or parameters ($param, Bindings) and keep the query text constant.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/opencypher-parameterized-queries.html

### `AF-GDB-024` — Neo4j plan uses AllNodesScan or CartesianProduct (medium)

AllNodesScan reads every node; CartesianProduct multiplies two independent result sets.


Remediation: Add labels/indexed predicates and connect disconnected patterns.

Reference: https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/planning-and-tuning/operators/

### `AF-GDB-025` — Executed plan shows a high fan-out ratio (low)

An operator emitting at least 1000 rows per input row in an executed plan (profile/dynamic explain) points at a supernode or an unselective expansion.


Remediation: Filter edges before expanding, partition the supernode, or cap the expansion.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/access-graph-opencypher-explain.html
